meaning: to do something badly or carelessly in order to save time or money
example: The builders cut corners on safety, so the new bridge had to be repaired within a year.
origin: The exact origin is uncertain; one suggestion links it to taking shortcuts around the corners of a building or path

wrong_meanings.meaning: to cut paper neatly with scissors
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally, but the idiom describes doing work carelessly, not cutting objects

wrong_meanings.meaning: to take a shortcut through a park
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom refers to lowering quality, not choosing a faster physical route

wrong_meanings.meaning: to divide a cake into equal pieces
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has no connection to dividing food; it describes poor-quality work

explanation: 'Cut corners' means to do something in a cheap or hasty way that lowers quality, usually to save time or money. It is often used to criticise careless work.
